assertions.text: The impact of the break on the work-optional date is stated as a range or under more than one named scenario, not as a single revised date.
assertions.evidence: Section 4 gives named scenarios at two rates: "At 4.5% real: No break Dec 2032 | Break, back at $196,000 Oct 2034 | ...$150,000 May 2036 | ...$130,000 May 2037"; a second table repeats all four "At 2.5% real" (Mar 2034 / Feb 2036 / Sep 2038 / Jul 2040).

assertions.text: Outcomes are reported under at least two different investment-return assumptions, one materially more conservative than the base case.
assertions.evidence: Section 4 gives full outcome tables under "**At 4.5% real:**" (no break Dec 2032; break at $150k May 2036) and "**At 2.5% real:**" (Mar 2034; Sep 2038). Section 5 repeats re-entry scenarios at both rates ("At 2.5% real... **June 2041, age 53**").

assertions.text: Statutory or regulatory figures quoted in the document (tax brackets or deductions, contribution limits, subsidy or poverty-line thresholds, penalty rules) each carry a source and the date they were checked.
assertions.evidence: "I also used 2026 federal brackets, a $16,100 standard deduction, Colorado's 4.25% flat rate, and a federal poverty level of about $16,450" — no citation, no check date. Elsewhere only "As of my information" hedges the 400% cliff; no figure in the doc names a source or date verified.

assertions.text: The document names which accounts fund the break and in what order.
assertions.evidence: Section 1 names HYSA cash as primary ("The $103,700 covers the whole break") plus an ordered waterfall: "1. HYSA cash... 2. Taxable brokerage... 3. Roth IRA contribution basis, $54,000... 4. HSA... 5. Traditional 401(k). Last, and not in the base plan."

assertions.text: The funding plan either avoids early-withdrawal penalties on retirement accounts or, where a penalized withdrawal is contemplated, states the penalty and tax cost explicitly.
assertions.evidence: Base plan avoids it ("without touching the 401(k), and without a penalty"), and the contemplated case is priced: "Federal ordinary income tax at 12% | 1,200 / 10% early distribution penalty | 1,000 / Colorado 4.25% | 425 / Total | 2,625, or 26.2%".

assertions.text: Health coverage is priced for all 24 months of the break; no part of the break period is left with unpriced or unspecified coverage.
assertions.evidence: Three contiguous blocks span Aug 2027–Aug 2029: "international medical plan ... roughly $200/month, $1,600 for the eight months"; "Marketplace, Apr - Dec 2028 | 1,260"; "Marketplace, Jan - Aug 2029 | 3,280", plus travel medical 560 and medevac 600 → "Total | 11,300".

assertions.text: The document evaluates using the low-income break years for Roth conversion or capital-gains harvesting, reaching a stated recommendation (doing either, or explicitly not, with a reason).
assertions.evidence: Section 3: "**Convert about $19,675 from the traditional 401(k) to a Roth IRA in December 2028. Not more.**" and "**Do not harvest capital gains in 2028.** The room is better spent on the conversion" — with a rung-by-rung table of effective rates (6.2% at 150% FPL) as the reason.

assertions.text: The document connects the size or source of withdrawals and conversions during the break to health-insurance subsidy eligibility (income thresholds), rather than treating the two as independent.
assertions.evidence: Sec 3: "Both a Roth conversion and a harvested capital gain add to the same number: modified adjusted gross income. That number sets your health subsidy." Table maps conversions to 150/200/250/400% FPL rungs; waterfall notes Roth basis "does not count as income for the ACA at all."

assertions.text: The planning horizon extends to at least age 95.
assertions.evidence: "You want the plan to run to 95. If you stop at 48, that is a 47-year retirement, and the 25x rule is a 30-year rule" — followed by a withdrawal-rate table (4%→3%, $1.575M→$2.1M) and SS "$44,000 undiscounted across ages 67 to 95."

assertions.text: Downside outcomes are described in terms of what Maya would actually live on or do differently (spending level, break shortened, working longer), not solely as a portfolio survival or success percentage.
assertions.evidence: Downsides are lived, not survival rates: "The cut is the South America leg of Phase C, which saves about $14,500 and shortens the break by four months"; "do not buy the van. Rent, or shorten Phase C to eight months and re-enter in June 2029"; bad corner "puts you at work-optional at 53."

assertions.text: The document states at least one if-then rule with a numeric trigger and a defined checkpoint for delaying departure or cutting the break short.
assertions.evidence: "Gate 1, 1 April 2027... Total portfolio ≥ $780,000... If you breach it, **delay by twelve months rather than cancelling.**" Also "Gate 3, 1 February 2028... Cash remaining < $72,000... The cut is the South America leg of Phase C."

assertions.text: The document shows the effect on the plan of re-entering work later than planned or at lower pay than the base assumption.
assertions.evidence: "Sep 2029 at $130,000 | May 2037 | 49 / Mar 2030 at $150,000 (six-month search) | Jan 2037 | 48 / Mar 2030 at $130,000 (both go wrong) | Feb 2038 | 50" plus "At 2.5% real, the same four: September 2038, July 2040, July 2039, and June 2041, age 53."

assertions.text: The asset figures the document is built on agree, within rounding, with the balances in Maya's own records.
assertions.evidence: Matches records: "your $46,800 HYSA" → "$103,700 on 1 August 2027" (46,800+12×4,500+interest); "Roth IRA contribution basis, $54,000"; "your basis is 69.5% of value" (121,000/174,200); "your $740,000" ≈ 740,800 total; 401(k) 412k grows to "$459,000" by mid-2027.

assertions.text: The document names at least one specific item for Maya to verify with a licensed professional or the relevant official body — beyond a generic advice disclaimer.
assertions.evidence: "Confirm this with Connect for Health Colorado before you leave" (the return-from-abroad special enrollment period); also "Colorado has run state-level affordability programs... Check Connect for Health Colorado at enrollment." Named official body, named specific item.
